passage:
Counsellor’s note, Thursday. Wasim came in after lunch and sat with his bag on his lap. Three weeks ago he reported a lab-marks entry that had been changed, and the lab in-charge corrected it. Since then the class chat has stopped including him, someone wrote “informer” on the lab board, and two groups go quiet when he passes.
He said, “I keep thinking I should have said nothing.” He also said Samir, who sits beside him, still shares notes and eats lunch with him, and that this helps.
I told Wasim that reporting was not his fault and that the isolation is what needs dealing with. That afternoon I spoke to the head of department about the board and the chat. The head had the board wiped before the last class and said the class chat will be raised with the whole group tomorrow.
Next week I will meet Wasim again.
— College counsellor

qa.q: What did someone write on the lab board?
qa.a: Someone wrote “informer” on the lab board.

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling when he said he should have said nothing?
qa.a: Wasim was feeling lonely and doubtful about having reported, since he was being shut out by the class. It shows the isolation weighs heavily on him.

qa.q: What did the counsellor do that helped Wasim?
qa.a: The counsellor told Wasim that reporting was not his fault and took the board and the chat to the head of department that same afternoon. They also planned another meeting for next week.

qa.q: How might Samir's sitting beside Wasim matter to Wasim?
qa.a: Samir's sharing notes and eating lunch together shows Wasim is not alone. One ally can make the labelling and gossip easier to bear.

grounding: Shows a student isolated and labelled after reporting wrongdoing, with one ally and a counsellor's same-day action.

passage:
Thursday night. The whole class went quiet when I walked in. I reported the changed marks on Monday, and today nobody saved me a seat and my name was left off the project group. Somebody drew a rat on my notebook.
In the canteen I sat alone until Mahima put her tray down across from me and said, “I think you did the right thing.” She didn’t say anything else. I nearly cried into my tea.
I keep asking myself whether I’m a troublemaker. I’m still angry and scared. Tomorrow I’m going to show the counsellor the drawing. At least one person is on my side.
— Baljeet

qa.q: What did Mahima say to Baljeet in the canteen?
qa.a: Mahima said, “I think you did the right thing.”

qa.q: Why did Baljeet nearly cry into the tea?
qa.a: Baljeet had felt shut out all day, and one kind sentence from Mahima showed someone was on Baljeet's side. Relief and loneliness came together.

qa.q: What is Baljeet planning to do about the rat drawing, and why is it sensible?
qa.a: Baljeet plans to show the counsellor the drawing. Telling an adult who can act helps the retaliation stop.

qa.q: What might Mahima have been feeling when she sat down at Baljeet's table?
qa.a: Mahima may have felt nervous about being seen with Baljeet but decided to be kind anyway. Saying so quietly and only once suggests a careful, brave gesture.

grounding: Shows a student who reported wrongdoing being isolated, gossiped about and labelled, and helped by one ally.

passage: Jomon, you told your manager about the fake overtime claims and now nobody eats with you? Sit. Your Madhuri aunty knows this feeling. In 1998, as a young nurse in Thrissur, I reported that a senior was taking medicines home from the ward store. The inquiry was quiet, and she was transferred. But the ward never forgave me. Tea-break conversations stopped when I walked in. Someone left a note in my locker: 'Snake.' My review called me 'difficult'. I nearly resigned. Then one ward aide, Thankamma chechi, started sitting next to me at lunch every single day, saying nothing special, just sitting. It was enough. One person, Jomon. Find your Thankamma. And be one for someone else.

qa.q: What was written on the note in young Madhuri's locker?
qa.a: 'Snake.'

qa.q: How did young Madhuri feel in the months after reporting?
qa.a: Isolated and hurt, close to resigning as conversations stopped when she walked in.

qa.q: What choice in the story made the isolation bearable?
qa.a: Thankamma chechi choosing to sit beside her at lunch every day, one quiet ally.

qa.q: What might Thankamma chechi have risked by sitting with Madhuri?
qa.a: Being gossiped about or isolated too, which makes her quiet support brave.

grounding: An aunt recalls being quietly ostracised after reporting wrongdoing, and how one ally made it bearable.

passage: Sunaina had reported the mess manager for pocketing money from the hostel food budget two weeks before her final exams. Now, in the small hostel of forty girls, nobody sat with her. The manager was related to half the staff, and the rumour went round that Sunaina was 'a troublemaker who wanted free food'. Someone scrawled 'chugli', telltale, on her door. With exams ten days away and the Wi-Fi 'mysteriously' off on her floor, she studied by the corridor light, eyes stinging. Then Lakshmi, from the room opposite, knocked at eleven at night with two cups of tea and her notes. 'You were right. I'm studying with you till the exams.' They sat on the floor till one. The next morning Lakshmi also wrote a supporting statement to the warden.

qa.q: What was scrawled on Sunaina's door?
qa.a: 'Chugli', meaning telltale.

qa.q: How did Sunaina feel studying by the corridor light?
qa.a: Isolated and worn down, eyes stinging, shut out by the other girls with exams close.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi do that mattered?
qa.a: She studied with Sunaina every night and wrote a supporting statement to the warden, standing openly beside her.

qa.q: How might the other girls see Sunaina after the rumour?
qa.a: Many seem to believe she is a troublemaker, swayed by the manager's links to the staff.

grounding: A student who reported wrongdoing is quietly isolated before exams, and one ally makes a great difference.

passage: In the coaching centre in Kota, word spread fast that Mahima was the one who'd told the director about Sir leaking test papers to his favourite batch. By Monday, the girls at her table had moved to another bench. In the group chat, someone posted a snake symbol every time she wrote. The teacher she'd reported now marked her answers harshly, and nobody said anything. Mahima started eating lunch alone in the stairwell, telling herself she didn't care. On Thursday, Aditi from the back bench sat down beside her with a lunchbox. 'I saw the leaked papers too. I should have said something. Want half my paratha?' Mahima laughed, suddenly teary. That afternoon the two of them went to the director together to report the harsh marking.

qa.q: Where did Mahima eat lunch after being frozen out?
qa.a: Alone in the stairwell.

qa.q: What did Mahima feel when Aditi sat down beside her?
qa.a: A sudden rush of relief and gratitude, laughing and teary after days of isolation.

qa.q: How did Aditi's support turn into action?
qa.a: She admitted she'd seen the leaks too, and went with Mahima to the director to report the harsh marking.

qa.q: How might the girls who moved benches see Mahima?
qa.a: As a traitor to the batch, following the group's quiet retaliation rather than thinking about the leaks.

grounding: A student who reported a teacher's wrongdoing faces quiet social retaliation, and one ally changes everything.

passage:
"Is this seat free?" Hemant asked. The three at the table glanced at one another. "Saving it," said Rishabh, not looking up.
Hemant moved to the corner. Two tables away someone muttered, "That's the one who got Nikhil sir suspended."
"Nikhil sir was taking money for marks," Hemant said, to nobody.
Leela set her tray down opposite him. "Mind if I sit?"
"You sure? They'll talk about you too."
"Let them. Did you eat anything today?"
"No. Nobody's said a word to me since Monday. Not rude. Just nothing. They stop talking when I walk in."
"I know. I've watched it." She pushed half her samosa across. "For what it's worth, you did the right thing. My brother paid him last year. He still feels sick about it."
Hemant laughed, shakily. "One person. That's all it takes, huh?"
"Also, the grievance committee handles retaliation. I'll come with you to the dean tomorrow if you want."
"Yeah. Okay."

qa.q: What was Nikhil sir doing, according to Hemant?
qa.a: Nikhil sir was taking money for marks.

qa.q: How was Hemant feeling as he sat alone in the corner?
qa.a: He felt isolated and hurt, since nobody had spoken to him since Monday, though he still believed the report was right.

qa.q: How did Leela support Hemant in practical ways?
qa.a: She sat with him, shared food, told him he did the right thing, and offered to go with him to the dean tomorrow.

qa.q: Why might Rishabh and the others be avoiding Hemant?
qa.a: They may fear being linked to him, or feel loyal to the teacher, so quiet avoidance feels safer than taking a side.

grounding: Shows a student isolated and gossiped about after reporting wrongdoing, and how much one ally's support matters.
